message.content:
**First Studio Ghibli film to win the Japan Academy Film Prize for Picture of the Year**

| Award year | Winning film |
|------------|--------------|
| **1998**   | *Princess Mononoke* (Japanese title: *Mononoke‑Hime*) |

*Princess Mononoke* received the prestigious “Picture of the Year” honor at the 21st Japan Academy Prize ceremony held in 1998. It was the first time a Studio Ghibli feature had taken home the top prize at Japan’s national film awards.

---

### How its box‑office success boosted Ghibli’s international popularity

| Aspect | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Domestic box‑office record** | *Princess Mononoke* earned roughly ¥12.9 billion (≈ US$120 million) in Japan, becoming the highest‑grossing Japanese film of its time and the most successful Ghibli production until *Spirited Away*. |
| **Worldwide reach** | The film sold about 1.5 million tickets in Japan alone and grossed around US$140 million worldwide when released in select markets (including the U.S., Canada, Australia, and parts of Europe). |
| **Distribution breakthrough** | Its commercial triumph convinced Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures to partner with Ghibli for North American distribution. Disney handled the U.S. theatrical release in 2002, followed by home‑video and television rights. |
| **European penetration** | Success in Japan made the film attractive to European distributors. It opened the door for releases in France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the Netherlands, often accompanied by localized dubbing and subtitling. |
| **Brand credibility** | The combination of critical acclaim (winning Picture of the Year) and massive ticket sales positioned Ghibli as a serious contender on the world stage. Distributors began to see Ghibli titles as commercially viable, leading to broader releases for subsequent films (*Howl’s Moving Castle*, *Kiki’s Delivery Service*, etc.). |
| **Long‑term ripple effect** | The confidence gained from *Princess Mononoke*’s success enabled Ghibli to secure larger budgets for later projects, notably *Spirited Away* (2001), which would go on to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature in 2003. |
| **Merchandising & licensing** | The film’s popularity spurred a wave of licensed products—action figures, apparel, art books—which were marketed worldwide, further cementing Ghibli’s global brand. |

In short, *Princess Mononoke*’s record‑breaking domestic earnings and its status as Japan’s best‑picture winner gave Studio Ghibli the clout to negotiate favorable distribution deals abroad, broaden its audience base, and lay the groundwork for the worldwide phenomenon that would follow with *Spirited Away* and beyond.
